Shane Cullen, 31, died after being assaulted at Blues Cabaret and Karaoke Bar on Bow Street, Ashton-under-Lyne, on 11 July. Greater Manchester Police (GMP) told a Tameside Council licensing committee hearing that management did not shut off the music, stop alcohol sales, raise the lights or evacuate the premises "despite the severity of the situation". After the incident, GMP applied for a review of the bar's licence. In a statement served ahead of the council licensing committee meeting on Thursday, PC Craig Foley said the force had serious concerns, including about "significant failings in management, supervision, compliance and leadership". Image source, GMP Image caption, Shane Cullen's family say he was a "gentle giant" and would be "sadly missed" Foley said door supervisors outside had "no effective view" of events occurring inside. A bouncer was also noted to have witnessed a separate assault outside the bar "without intervening or acting". Foley said that officers attended the bar and helped clear a space for paramedics to begin commencing CPR. He wrote: "Despite the severity of the situation, alcohol sales continued, music continued to be played and customers continued dancing and congregating around the area where officers were admin

She was taken into the bedroom of Al Masri's house in Abbey Hey were Al Masri raped her, while his friend remained in the room. The woman's boyfriend had contacted police and shared her location. title: Trains returning to normal after Manchester power disruption

input.summary: Rail services were returning to normal after an outage in Manchester on Thursday caused major disruption

On Wednesday (August 12), sky watchers across parts of Europe will be treated to an impressive celestial spectacle While those in parts of Spain, northern Portugal and Iceland are set to witness a total eclipse that will transform day into night. In the UK, however, only a partial eclipse will be visible - but there's something special about this one According to Royal Museums Greenwich, next week's partial solar eclipse will be the most coverage seen from the UK and Ireland since the 1999 eclipse A solar eclipse takes place when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth, casting a shadow on Earth. Depending on where you are in the UK, up to 96 per cent of the Sun will be covered by the Moon The UK last witnessed a solar eclipse in March 2025, but only around 30-40 per cent of the Sun was covered by the Moon. input.evidence_text: Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 07:28, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 07:28, 08 Aug 2026 The UK's biggest solar eclipse in 27 years is fast approaching. On Wednesday (August 12), sky watchers across parts of Europe will be treated to an impressive celestial spectacle While those in parts of Spain, northern Portugal and Iceland are set to witness a total eclipse that will transform day into night. In the UK, however, only a partial eclipse will be visible - but there's something special about this one According to Royal Museums Greenwich, next week's partial solar eclipse will be the most coverage seen from the UK and Ireland since the 1999 eclipse A solar eclipse takes place when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth, casting a shadow on Earth. Depending on where you are in the UK, up to 96 per cent of the Sun will be covered by the Moon The UK last witnessed a solar eclipse in March 2025, but only around 30-40 per cent of the Sun was covered by the Moon. input.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk.
